findings.claim: Without a surrogate, the collector always uses contractless mode and never reads attributes on T. `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember(Name)]`, `[IgnoreDataMember]`, `[MessagePackObject]`/`[Key]` and `[IgnoreMember]` are all ignored. The acceptance criteria require T's attributes to be honoured. Concrete input: a referenced type `[DataContract] class MyObject { [DataMember(Name="a")] public int Included {get;set;} public int NotAMember {get;set;} }`. On head the generated formatter serializes `NotAMember` under the key "NotAMember" and `Included` under "Included" instead of "a". That breaks wire compatibility with the dynamic resolver, and members the author excluded are serialized anyway.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptTests.DataContractOnReferencedTypeIsHonoured. It compiles ProjectA with the [DataContract] type into a metadata reference and runs MessagePackGenerator on ProjectB with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]. It asserts no generated source mentions NotAMember. Expected to fail on head.

findings.claim: IsPartial checks only the formatter's own declaration. Consider a formatter nested in a non-partial containing type, for example `public class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] internal partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> {} }`. It passes the check, and the template then emits the nesting `partial class Outer { partial class F ... }`. The result is CS0260 (missing partial modifier on Outer) instead of a MsgPack019 diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptTests.FormatterNestedInNonPartialTypeDoesNotProduceCS0260. It asserts that the post-generation compilation has no CS0260. Expected to fail on head.

findings.claim: No accessibility check is made on the formatter class itself. A `private partial class F` nested in another type is accepted and registered in the generated resolver. The resolver cannot instantiate it, so compilation fails with CS0122 (inaccessible) instead of a generator diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Collect validates only IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(type, formatter) for the data type, never the formatter's own accessibility relative to the resolver. Compare with MsgPack012 handling for data types.

findings.claim: GetInstanceMembers keeps only the most-derived member of each name. Take a derived class that overrides only the getter (`public override int X { get => ...; }`) of a base read-write property. Its IPropertySymbol has SetMethod == null, so IsPublicReadWrite returns false and the base's writable X is shadowed by the `seen` set. The member is silently dropped from the contractless contract, although the property is writable through the base setter.

receipt_plan.detail: GetInstanceMembers adds the derived override to `seen` before visiting the base. IsPublicReadWrite then requires property.SetMethod to be non-null, and an override with only a get accessor has none.
